blocks.content: The parliamentary system of government is one in which the executive is responsible to the legislature for its policies and acts.

rows: Single executive (President is both head of State and Government)
Executive is responsible to the Legislature
Executive is not responsible to the Legislature
Double membership (Ministers belong to both Legislature and Executive)
Single membership (Ministers cannot be members of the Legislature)
Prime Minister is the primary leader and center of power
President is the primary leader and center of power
Lower House (Lok Sabha) can be dissolved by Executive
Lower House (House of Representatives) cannot be dissolved by President

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Articles 74 and 75 provide for a parliamentary system at the Centre, while Articles 163 and 164 provide for it in the states.
The executive is responsible to the legislature for its policies and acts, making it a responsible government.
The President is the nominal executive (de jure executive), whereas the Prime Minister is the real executive (de facto executive).
Ministers hold double membership, meaning they are members of both the legislature and the executive.
The parliamentary system is also known as Cabinet Government or the Westminster Model of Government.
Article 75 explicitly lays down that the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha (House of the People).
Unlike the British system where Parliament is supreme, the Indian Parliament is not a sovereign body due to a written Constitution, federalism, and judicial review.
In India, the Prime Minister must be a member of either the Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha; if not a member at appointment, they must get elected within six months.
